question: Should the fixed -3-point offset be accepted for all stacked menu-bar title size variants based on the Regular native proof, or should those variants receive visual confirmation first?
rationale: The patch is mechanically narrow and proven for the reported Regular layout, but a constant visual adjustment can have different perceived alignment at other supported title sizes.

options.title: Capture remaining size variants
options.body: Add redacted native before/after captures for the other supported stacked size variants, then merge if their visual centering remains acceptable.

options.title: Accept the scoped visual risk
options.body: Merge based on the directly demonstrated Regular layout and treat any size-specific adjustment as a follow-up if users report it.

recommendation.title: Capture remaining size variants
recommendation.body: Add redacted native before/after captures for the other supported stacked size variants, then merge if their visual centering remains acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository ownership is the only available reliable routing signal for the visual acceptance decision.
